features.headline: 'He's like f—-ing Busquets!' - Jules Ahoka is making an unlikely Premier League rise
features.desc: Making his first Premier League start on Saturday, Sunderland's Jules Ahoka made playing at Villa Park look like a stroll in the park. The 20-year-old Congolese midfielder looked at home as he helped the Black Cats earn a valuable 0-0 draw.
body: Making his first Premier League start on Saturday, Sunderland's Jules Ahoka made playing at Villa Park look like a stroll in the park.

The 20-year-old Congolese midfielder looked at home as he helped the Black Cats earn a valuable 0-0 draw, having stepped in for the injured Granit Xhaka, playing the full 90 minutes, and building on his excellent showing in the 1-0 victory over Chelsea before the international break.

He made 10 interceptions and clearances combined — more together than any other player on the pitch — and made several progressive passes to suggest that he's more than a one-dimensional midfield destroyer.
Ahoka's performance was busy, proactive, without the youngster ever looking hurried or hassled.

It was an impressive feat against an Aston Villa side who hadn't lost in their previous six Premier League games, and he'd cut a similarly unruffled figure against Chelsea, after replacing Xhaka in the fourth minute.
His teammate, Belgium international Thomas Meunier, couldn't hide how impressed he was with his young teammate's composed performance.
"Six months ago, he was playing in Belgium for Royal Antwerp," Meunier told journalists, "and now he's like f—-ing Busquets," he continued, referencing the legendary Spain and Barcelona midfielder.
It was a playful comment, but hyperbolically generous one as well, with Meunier acknowledging some of Ahoka's subtle qualities which are appreciated by his teammates.

Like the FIFA World Cup-winning Spaniard, Ahoka looks particularly comfortable receiving the ball in a crowded midfield — a dream for a defence finding themselves under pressure and looking for a favourable outball.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here, as this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
Skubal to NYM | Peralta to BAL Sato to CHC | Gray to MIN | Bauers to BOS
The deal: Three years, $30 million (with opt-out after second year)
Tyler Stephenson has been a fixture behind the plate for the Cincinnati Reds since his rookie season in 2021, a steady if unspectacular presence.

The Reds bring him back on a reasonable deal that will keep Stephenson in Cincinnati for at least two more seasons — keeping the catching position solidified until the team's top prospect, power-hitting Alfredo Duno, is ready to take over.

With Stephenson, you know what you're going to get: He essentially has been a league-average hitter over the past three seasons, maybe a little better going by wRC+ or similar metrics, hitting for some power and drawing enough walks to keep his on-base percentage above water.
He's entering his age-30 season, so not a lot should change in his offensive profile in the next two years.

The knock is his defense, where he consistently has ranked near the bottom in Statcast's pitch-framing metric. He ranked 55th out of 56 regular catchers in 2026 at minus-9 runs saved; he ranked 50th out of 57 in 2025; and 45th out of 58 in 2024.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
Right-hander Freddy Peralta and the Baltimore Orioles are in agreement on a five-year, $125 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Left-hander Kris Bubic and the Cleveland Guardians are in agreement on a one-year, $17.5 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
The Chicago Cubs have reached an agreement with Japanese Central League MVP Teruaki Sato on a six-year, $120 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Star Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira and the Toronto Blue Jays are in agreement on a five-year, $80 million contract with an opt-out after the third season, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
Catcher Tyler Stephenson and the Cincinnati Reds are in agreement on a three-year, $30 million contract with an opt-out after the second season, pending physical, sources tell ESPN.
The Chicago White Sox are in agreement with free agent outfielder Tyrone Taylor on a two-year, $17 million contract, sources confirmed to ESPN.
Infielder Ha-Seong Kim and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a one-year, $5 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
The Chicago Cubs have agreed to a five-year, $120 million contract with free agent pitcher Trevor Rogers, sources familiar with the situation told ESPN.

features.headline: Tyrese, Jade Haliburton announce they are expecting their first child
features.desc: The couple wed in August after seven years of dating and announced the news that they're expecting on Instagram.
body: Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton and his wife, Jade, are expecting their first child, the couple announced Tuesday in a joint post on Instagram.
They shared the news with a photoshoot that featured their apricot labradoodle, Ames, wearing an apron that said "Big Brother" and their ultrasound image.

The comments were flooded with congratulations from athletes and teams such as gymnast Simone Biles, Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark, New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart, Los Angeles Sparks center Cameron Brink, San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle, the Fever and the Pacers.
Haliburton's current and former teammates Andrew Nembhard, James Johnson and Jay Huff also chimed in, as did the Golden State Warriors' Georges Niang and Charlotte Hornets' Grant Williams.
The post's caption reads: "Baby Hali. Spring 2027."

The Haliburtons wed in August after getting engaged in July 2025 and being together for seven years. The couple met while attending Iowa State. Jade was a cheerleader, and Tyrese played two seasons with the Cyclones before being drafted in 2020.

The Pacers guard tore his right Achilles tendon in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, sidelining him for all of the 2025-26 season. He returned this season and averaged 21.8 points, 9.5 assists and 4.5 rebounds in four games until suffering a hamstring strain that has kept him out since Oct. 26.

features.headline: Rest-of-season rankings: Coleman surges among RBs, Taylor sinks
features.desc: Need to know how to value players from this point forward for production or trade discussions? Eric Karabell has you covered.
body: Which players are on the rise and which ones are falling, and what does it mean for their prospects for the rest of the season?

Dak Prescott is continuing his climb in the QB ranks. Jonah Coleman bursts into the top 10 among running backs, while Jonathan Taylor continues to slide. Things remain relatively steady among pass catchers.

Each week, Eric Karabell ranks players by position based on their fantasy football value for the rest of the 2026 season. Use the information to optimize players for their future potential and/or to gauge trade value. Eric's overall top 100 list can be found at the bottom of this column.
Rankings changes: Dak Prescott, boasting consecutive games with more than 34 fantasy points, moves back into the top 10.
Prescott enters Week 12 second to Joe Burrow in full-season QB scoring, but he is also the lone top-12 QB here yet to serve his bye week.
Josh Allen fell from the No. 1 spot a week ago, and then he scored fewer than 13 points for the second time in three games. Should Brock Purdy pass him? We are not there yet.

Patrick Mahomes also returns to the top 10, while Trevor Lawrence and Kirk Cousins leave. Cam Ward has become interesting for deep leaguers. We're not there yet with Justin Herbert or Anthony Richardson Sr.
Rankings changes: Standout Chuba Hubbard enters Week 12 as the No. 3 RB for the season, so we could no longer deny him a top-5 spot. Perhaps Bijan Robinson takes that spot back this coming week.

It sure didn't take rookie Jonah Coleman long to achieve a top-10 spot, while it took a long time for Jonathan Taylor to lose his. Emmett Johnson is a revelation, but his value depends on the health of Kenneth Walker III (groin).

features.headline: One trade ESPN experts would make before MLB lockout
features.desc: An MLB lockout is looming. Our experts suggest some last-minute deals.
body: Say it with us: Major League Baseball is about to shut down.
But wait! Before the lockout begins — which, if you haven't heard, is expected to happen Tuesday, Dec. 1, at 11:59 p.m. ET — there remains a lot of business to get done.
Although all the offseason free agent signings and trades won't be made in the next week, a lot of them will (and already have been).

While we wait for a potential flurry of moves, we asked our MLB experts to share one deal — specifically, a trade — they'd love to see made before the league goes dark. Here is how they responded, starting with a pair of swaps involving a Boston outfielder.
A year ago, such a paltry return would have been unthinkable for Duran, who generated 13.9 bWAR in 2024-25 thanks to a robust batting line (124 OPS+) and outstanding defensive metrics (32 DRS).
But his value cratered in 2026, as he mustered 0.4 bWAR and a 76 OPS+, rendering him a non-tender candidate with a projected $11 million arbitration salary looming.
Corbin Carroll anchors an Arizona outfield with reliably little else, and the contours of Chase Field would amplify Duran's propensity for doubles and triples. — Paul Hembekides
Phillies executive Dave Dombrowski led the Red Sox when the organization drafted Duran in 2018, but he was long gone by the time Duran became an All-Star in 2024.
Duran's 2026 campaign was obviously a struggle, and the Red Sox boast depth among their corner outfielders. The Phillies certainly do not.

With no immediate path to the rotation for 2025 first-round pick Wood, and no certainty that he remains on track for an eventual rotation spot, it would hardly be surprising to see the aggressive Dombrowski move another top prospect for immediate aid.
